items.title: AMD shares fell 10.88% on Friday as investors reassessed the semiconductor sector following Intel’s disappointing earnings and weaker-than-e
items.content_excerpt: AMD shares fell 10.88% on Friday as investors reassessed the semiconductor sector following Intel’s disappointing earnings and weaker-than-expected guidance. Intel’s results exposed two significant challenges that could also affect AMD: weakness in the PC market and insufficient server CPU production capacity despite strong demand. On the PC side, rising memory-chip prices are increasing computer costs and discouraging consumers and businesses from purchasing new devices. Corporate IT departments are also operating with tighter budgets, delaying laptop replacements and upgrades. This creates additional pressure on processor manufacturers that depend on PC sales for a significant portion of their revenue. The second concern involves the server market. Intel acknowledged that it cannot manufacture enough server processors to satisfy robust demand for CPUs, highlighting production constraints even as AI infrastructure investment drives demand for computing capacity. $AMD $INTC

items.title: Apple reclaimed its position as the world’s most valuable publicly traded company on Friday, overtaking Nvidia as growing concerns over aggr
items.content_excerpt: Apple reclaimed its position as the world’s most valuable publicly traded company on Friday, overtaking Nvidia as growing concerns over aggressive AI spending triggered a rotation toward companies with stronger balance sheets and more disciplined capital allocation. Despite falling 1.2%, Apple ended the session with a $5.03 trillion market capitalization, surpassing Nvidia’s $4.93 trillion after its shares dropped 4.2%. The shift comes amid mounting skepticism over returns on massive AI infrastructure investments, intensified by quarterly updates from Intel and Amazon following disappointing reactions to results from Alphabet and Meta. Alphabet has fallen 18.6% over the past month, Meta 15.2%, Intel nearly 30% in a single session, and Nvidia 10% over the past month. Apple has emerged as a relative safe haven among the Magnificent Seven because of its more measured infrastructure spending. Its shares are up 27% year to date and 3% over the past month. $AAPL $NVDA

Analyst targets aren’t guarantees—and they’re generally 12-month views. But dismissing every bullish assessment because the stock had an ugly session makes little sense. Volatility comes with the territory. My conviction rests on the business. 💪📈

items.title: $APLD Wes Cummins Returns to CNBC Monday His Previous Appearances Have Coincided With BILLIONS in New Deals and Major Stock Moves. Could Ano
items.content_excerpt: $APLD Wes Cummins Returns to CNBC Monday His Previous Appearances Have Coincided With BILLIONS in New Deals and Major Stock Moves. Could Another Mega Announcement Be Coming? My best guess - at about 8 AM on Monday $APLD announces its sixth major AI factory in the US - in Mobile, Alabama. I have no one-sided information about this, but $APLD has filed a series of corporate filings in Alabama and Delaware, which I’ve discussed in prior posts, indicating that it has formed property owning LLC for a Mobile, Alabama AI factory, with many buildings. Wes is scheduled to appear on CNBC’s Squawk on the Street Monday, November 2, at 10:25 a.m. ET. This is worth watching closely. Wes’s previous appearances have repeatedly followed major corporate developments, including multibillion-dollar hyperscaler agreements, financing initiatives, and strategic expansion announcements. The timing of Wes’s Monday appearance raises an intriguing question: Is $APLD preparing to announce another major investment, financing commitment, or hyperscaler deal? Look at the history. In June 2025, Wes appeared following the announcement of the $7 billion $CRWV agreement for Polaris Forge 1 in Ellendale, ND. In October, he discussed the $5 billion Polaris Forge 2 hyperscaler lease and financing capacity which we now know is with $ORCL. In December, he addressed the proposed CHRN separation - which has now landed $MSFT as a client. In May 2026, he returned following the $7.5 billion Polaris Forge 3 agreement for Center, ND which we now know is with $META. That’s $19.5 BILLION in major lease agreements associated with just three of his previous CNBC appearances. Importantly, those deals were announced before the interviews, not unveiled live on television. The stock-price history is equally compelling. $APLD surged approximately 48% when the original $CRWV deal was announced and gained another 29% the day after Wes’s CNBC appearance. Following the May 2026 Polaris Forge 3 announcement, $APLD shares jumped approximately 22% in the next trading session, followed by an additional 8.5% gain on his interview date. Not every appearance resulted in a rally, but these examples demonstrate the enormous potential market impact of new hyperscaler commitments. My takeaway: Monday’s appearance deserves serious attention. With APLD’s expanding development pipeline, growing hyperscaler relationships, and enormous capital requirements, another major lease, strategic investment, or financing announcement is a realistic possibility. There’s no confirmation that anything new will be announced, and an interview alone doesn’t establish the odds. But given Wes’s track record of appearing on CNBC around transformative corporate developments, I wouldn’t dismiss the timing as coincidence. Monday could be very interesting for $APLD shareholders. My best guess is a big announcement is coming. With so much downward movement, $APLD stock is like a coiled spring. And Wes and his President Jason did not buy $6.7 million of $APLD common stock a few weeks ago for fun. I strongly suspect something is brewing.

items.content_excerpt: Oct 30 Market Wrap: Tech Rout vs. Macro Bull Case $QQQ fell 3.5% to $690.49 ( $SPY S&P 500 -1.82%). Down ~9.5% from its $762.86 peak, which is QQQ's 3rd correction of the year, trailing deeper pullbacks in March (-12.2%) and July (-11.3%). $GOOG (-$9.1B Q3 FCF) & $AMZN (-$42.4B TTM FCF) flipped cash-flow negative on massive AI capex. $INTC plunged 28.6% on weak Q4 guidance. Strait of Hormuz oil spikes + a record $6.3B Binance hack rattled risk appetite. Classic rotation out of tech into cash-flowing value (Energy +1.91%), compounded by pre-midterm de-risking after a strong YTD run. The Fed & Rate Thesis: Pushing the next hike to Jan & cutting hikes #3 & #4 is bullish for the broad market & cyclicals. The catch for QQQ: With Big Tech borrowing to fund AI at ~4% rates, tech multiples won't rebound until AI spend proves its ROI. Do you think tech AI will pay out?

items.content_excerpt: S&P Global Ratings downgraded its outlook on Meta to negative from stable, citing uncertainty over prolonged AI infrastructure spending and deteriorating free cash flow. The agency expects 2026 capex of approximately $140 billion, within Meta’s revised $135–145 billion guidance, rising sharply to more than $225 billion in 2027 and $252 billion in 2028, well above previous estimates. S&P now projects free cash flow deficits of $22 billion in 2026, $71 billion in 2027 and $39 billion in 2028, reversing its previous expectation of a return to positive cash flow. The agency sees greater uncertainty around Meta’s ability to monetize AI investments through improved advertising and agentic applications such as Muse, while competitors are already generating revenue by leasing computing capacity. Meta’s Q3 2026 revenue grew 26.1%, with advertising revenue up 25.9%, but free cash flow turned negative by $2.1 billion as capex reached $34.9 billion. $META

items.title: $APLD Wes Cummins Returns to CNBC Monday His Previous Appearances Have Coincided With BILLIONS in New Deals and Major Stock Moves. Could Ano
items.content_excerpt: $APLD Wes Cummins Returns to CNBC Monday His Previous Appearances Have Coincided With BILLIONS in New Deals and Major Stock Moves. Could Another Mega Announcement Be Coming? My best guess - at about 8 AM on Monday $APLD announces its sixth major AI factory in the US - in Mobile, Alabama. I have no one-sided information about this, but $APLD has filed a series of corporate filings in Alabama and Delaware, which I’ve discussed in prior posts, indicating that it has formed property owning LLC for a Mobile, Alabama AI factory, with many buildings. Wes is scheduled to appear on CNBC’s Squawk on the Street Monday, November 2, at 10:25 a.m. ET. This is worth watching closely. Wes’s previous appearances have repeatedly followed major corporate developments, including multibillion-dollar hyperscaler agreements, financing initiatives, and strategic expansion announcements. The timing of Wes’s Monday appearance raises an intriguing question: Is $APLD preparing to announce another major investment, financing commitment, or hyperscaler deal? Look at the history. In June 2025, Wes appeared following the announcement of the $7 billion $CRWV agreement for Polaris Forge 1 in Ellendale, ND. In October, he discussed the $5 billion Polaris Forge 2 hyperscaler lease and financing capacity which we now know is with $ORCL. In December, he addressed the proposed CHRN separation - which has now landed $MSFT as a client. In May 2026, he returned following the $7.5 billion Polaris Forge 3 agreement for Center, ND which we now know is with $META. That’s $19.5 BILLION in major lease agreements associated with just three of his previous CNBC appearances. Importantly, those deals were announced before the interviews, not unveiled live on television. The stock-price history is equally compelling. $APLD surged approximately 48% when the original $CRWV deal was announced and gained another 29% the day after Wes’s CNBC appearance. Following the May 2026 Polaris Forge 3 announcement, $APLD shares jumped approximately 22% in the next trading session, followed by an additional 8.5% gain on his interview date. Not every appearance resulted in a rally, but these examples demonstrate the enormous potential market impact of new hyperscaler commitments. My takeaway: Monday’s appearance deserves serious attention. With APLD’s expanding development pipeline, growing hyperscaler relationships, and enormous capital requirements, another major lease, strategic investment, or financing announcement is a realistic possibility. There’s no confirmation that anything new will be announced, and an interview alone doesn’t establish the odds. But given Wes’s track record of appearing on CNBC around transformative corporate developments, I wouldn’t dismiss the timing as coincidence. Monday could be very interesting for $APLD shareholders. My best guess is a big announcement is coming. With so much downward movement, $APLD stock is like a coiled spring. And Wes and his President Jason did not buy $6.7 million of $APLD common stock a few weeks ago for fun. I strongly suspect something is brewing.

items.title: Google is in preliminary talks with the U.S. Department of Defense to support data security for the $185 billion Golden Dome missile-defense
items.content_excerpt: Google is in preliminary talks with the U.S. Department of Defense to support data security for the $185 billion Golden Dome missile-defense program, marking its first known involvement in President Trump’s flagship initiative. Discussions focus on deploying Google’s data storage, networking and cybersecurity infrastructure to protect military command-and-control communications if conventional ground networks or cellular towers are compromised. The Pentagon is developing a multi-company consortium that could include Google spin-off Aalyria Technologies. The initiative would complement a broader defense command-and-control architecture being developed by Palantir, Anduril and SpaceX, integrating military hardware, radar networks and weapons systems across the armed forces. The talks remain preliminary, with no final decisions on the consortium’s structure or participants. $GOOGL

We’re highly diversified across asset classes, and a significant portion of our capital goes into lower-beta investments because our depositors prioritize stability, low volatility, and consistent returns. That said, we’re also taking advantage of this broader market selloff to deploy capital into high-quality, higher beta companies at attractive valuations. This is exactly the kind of opportunity disciplined institutional investors look for. While fear and short-term sentiment drive many retail investors to sell, long-term investors with capital to deploy can take advantage of these pullbacks to build positions in high-quality companies at more attractive valuations. In my view, $RKLB is one of those opportunities. The fundamentals haven’t changed, but the prices certainly have. And that’s where opportunities are created.

items.title: S&P Dow Jones Indices selected Okta to join the S&P 500 ahead of the market open on November 4, replacing Kenvue, which is preparing
items.content_excerpt: S&P Dow Jones Indices selected Okta to join the S&P 500 ahead of the market open on November 4, replacing Kenvue, which is preparing to be acquired by Kimberly-Clark pending completion of the transaction. The inclusion represents a significant institutional milestone for Okta and is expected to generate additional buying demand from passive index funds and ETFs that must purchase shares to replicate the benchmark. The reshuffle also triggers changes across other U.S. equity indices. Glaukos will move from the S&P SmallCap 600 to the S&P MidCap 400, replacing Okta, while McGrath RentCorp will take Glaukos’ former position in the SmallCap 600. McGrath shares initially gained 2.8% following the announcement. Separately, aerospace and defense supplier Loar Holdings rose 3.5% in after-hours trading after being selected to join the S&P SmallCap 600, replacing LiveRamp, which is being acquired by advertising group Publicis Groupe in a deal expected to close shortly. $OKTA $SPX

items.title: UK investors: most normal UK brokers won't sell you many US-listed income ETFs like $SCHD, $VOO or $QQQI, because they don't have th
items.content_excerpt: UK investors: most normal UK brokers won't sell you many US-listed income ETFs like $SCHD, $VOO or $QQQI, because they don't have the UK key information documents (KIDs) the rules require. There is a legal way in, though. Some US brokers that accept UK clients let you buy these funds directly. You open the account in USD and fill in a W-8BEN form so US tax on dividends is withheld at the treaty rate instead of the full rate. Before you jump in, three things are worth knowing: 1. Currency risk: you're holding USD. 2. These funds aren't held in an ISA wrapper, so UK tax applies. 3. Check the broker's fees and how it protects your money. Bookmark this if you've been wondering why you can't find these funds on your UK app. Research tools only, not financial advice. Capital at risk. $SPY

items.content_excerpt: @Natedawg32 $SPYI $QQQI hold the index and sell index call options, and the premium funds the payout. items.content_excerpt: Stifel has downgraded Whirlpool Corporation to sell from hold. “We contend WHR is losing market share in the key U.S. market. Losses could potentially accelerate given announced pricing to offset inflation (resin, steel), competitor incentives, limited appliance brand loyalty, and weaker WHR brand demographics,” wrote analyst W. Andrew Carter in a Tuesday note. Stifel also reduced its target price for the home appliance company to $20 from $30, implying a 27.1% downside from Tuesday’s close. The firm also lowered its FY28 EBITDA to $815 million from $872 million for the company. Challenges Whirlpool Corporation outlined in the third-quarter are “likely to accelerate” Carter added. The stock fell more than 2% in late morning trading on Wednesday. $WHR
